tips.comment: I expect Court In A Storm to romp home in this race. Convincing winner at Limerick, and this longer trip shouldn't be an issue.

Everyonesgame was 2nd in a point, won his first bumper, and won three times over hurdles to reach a hurdles mark of 132. His jumping has yet to convince in two chases. He was last of 3 at Plumpton, but he was moving into contention three lengths behind in 3rd place when he made a bad mistake and unseated three out at Kempton last time. Off the same mark of 117, he has every chance of redeeming himself over fences at Hereford.
Discounting his last effort at Chepstow after a 6-month break, he has run well in events at this level and distance before. The likeliest contender to take on the short favorite here.

Has now dropped to a nice-looking mark, with a decent jockey booked in Jonathan Burke. Amazingly, this is the jockey's first-ever ride for this stable. I think this looks like an eye-catching jockey booking. He's still a maiden over fences but ran a cracker off this mark at Ffos Las on ground softer than ideal. He finished a very close-up 2nd behind Alcedo, beaten just a neck by the winner. No disgrace there, given that horse was well in off his current mark. He's had 2 lesser runs since, both at this track, but neither over suitable trips. He drops back to the correct trip this time. He won over this C&D over hurdles back in October off this exact same mark. He's bred to make a chaser. He won his sole P2P run. Admittedly, he was booked for 2nd when Life In The Park fell at the last fence. To be fair, LITP is a 140+ rated performer under rules, so still a solid run. This looks easier than the last race he contested.
Travelled strongly into the race and then was not given a hard time at all on return to action. This looks a very winnable race for this horse, if improving fitness.

This looks like a good bit of value. This horse stepped up on his hurdling form after being fitted with a tongue tie on chase debut and seemingly bumped into one that day. He is dropped in trip here after looking in need of a shorter distance the last two times, and this will not take too much winning.

Pittsbug looks like a solid contender at Hereford on Thursday 10th, and here's why he's got a genuine chance to win: Won last time out at Market Rasen (17.2f, good to firm) just 15 days ago in a 6-runner handicap chase. He is only 4lb for that win, which still leaves him well treated on old form. His mark of 83 is still very workable for a horse with winning experience and carries 11st 11lb. Ridden again by Freddie Mitchell, who claims a handy 5lb, effectively softening that rise in the weights. That makes a real difference in a tight handicap like this. Race conditions, good ground, suit him well. Last win came from good to firm, so current going is ideal. He ticks all the boxes: recent win, solid weight, right ground, distance form, and jockey value compared to others needing to bounce back or prove themselves. He comes as the form horse and deserves to be the favorite. Good luck.

The Sarah-Jayne Davies trained Time To Dazzle has probably been priced up on his last 3 runs PPF. However, he is top-rated on 86 today, and if showing the same form as when 2nd in a Ludlow 2m Chase off 96 and his hurdle win off 95, I'm hoping he can bag one of the 3 places at huge odds in an ordinary looking Class 5 2m chase handicap.

Possibly not as effective on quick ground than soft, but has won on genuine good ground on the flat. Comes here from an attractive mark as he was rated in the 80s on the flat, and when he won over hurdles on his stable debut less than a year ago, several of the horses he beat off levels are now running off marks 110+. So his 102 mark here looks a gimme. Loves it around here, already a course and distance winner, and ran well here last time out. With a jockey upgrade with Cobden taking over, I fully expect him to win.
Back in a weaker Class 5 event from his previous decent efforts at both 3 & 4 last time out. If he can jump a little more fluently than he did at Stratford last month, he should take all the beating.

Won a course and distance novice event last year here after a similar layoff and is now only 5 lbs higher than that success. Was narrowly defeated here since and looks ready for another crack at this course now.
Not a great return run at Carlisle last time out when beaten a long way out. Might just come on for that run. Gets all the allowances here and off bottom weight, should be in with a chance.

Grenardier comes in with a lower weight and could spring a surprise in this race. Though his form has been inconsistent, a recent second-place finish shows he has ability when things go right. With a modest rating and young jockey Daire McConville in the saddle, he might benefit from a tactical race or any mistakes from the favourites. He’s an interesting outsider who could pull off a shock if the conditions suit.

Has first start for 10 months. Has won after a break of 4-5 months previously, that being his win last time. Not seen since then, so presumably had issues. But if fit and well now, then has a chance in this against her own sex and dropped down to a mark of 82.
Mistral Blue has been dropped a lot by the BHB handicapper and surely will take advantage of a low mark of 93 tomorrow at Hereford. 7/2 a big price. Get on!

Trainers are getting wise now to just how good this 7lb claiming Conditional jockey is, and he's getting more rides now from stables who think they have already well-handicapped horses on their hands. This 6yo mare was in and around 100(ish) rated horses on debut in a bumper and races here off 92 with the jockey's 7lb claim making it even more appealing. The stable knows how to get their horses racing off good marks, and they tend to do well at the course too, so hopefully, the money will be down for this one.

The 6-year-old has shown limited performance over hurdles and has been out of action for 9 months, but she wasn't pushed hard during her recent handicap debut. Shane Quinlan, who has been in good form recently, will be in the saddle and offers a 3lb weight allowance. Given the current odds of 28/1, an each-way bet could yield a good return.

Jackie Can's two best runs have been on good ground, the latest over CD a fortnight ago. That was the first run since over 3 months off. The three runs before were all on soft or good to soft. Likely to have benefited from that latest run, and an even better effort looks on the cards in this moderate event.
Cave Article seems to have improved for fences and has been sent off favourite a few times. Has to be able to get close here.

His two best runs have been over course and distance at the back end of last year. He won one and finished a close second in his follow-up bid. He is now a pound lower than for that follow-up run and should be backed as a well-handicapped horse at a track he loves.

SINCHI ROCA has won a NH flat race at 2m. Also won a point-to-point race. A winner on his latest outing in a NH flat race over 2m at Taunton in February, winning easily. Course distance and going should suit and could well be able to go in again and win this race.

Although she has never run before Windsor Blue's pedigree really catches the eye and looks worth an interest each way at the price and hopefully the 8 runners remain for 3 places. She is by the brilliant national hunt sire Blue Bresil and out of a mare who is related to loads of winners including Cogry, Wyldello and the prolific mare Marello who won 11 races for the Reveley's back in the day.

Despite there being 8 runners in this Bumper, you're basically backing this one e/w to get in the first 3 in a 5 runner race since 3 of the field are 100/1+ horses. Sire students will certainly be aware that this horse's sire has been making great waves in recent times in the Bumper sphere, and I can't let him go unbacked at 40/1. The horse was going on debut last time out before being bumped and possibly spooked by that before dropping away. The trainer isn't one to give a horse a quiet run in a Bumper before going hurdling because virtually all of his horses are Bumper runners rather than hurdlers, and he's worth sticking with for now, I'd say.

Famoso loves to hear his feet rattle and definitely gets that here at Newton Abbot this afternoon. Not only that, but he is pretty consistent over the minimum 16f and receives 12lb from the favorite, and that swings it. The favorite will lead, which will suit my selection, and if this doesn't get too tactical, he can wait until late and hit the front.
Looks the type to improve for the run latest when finishing 4th after a mammoth layoff. Can build on that and certainly go close here at good-looking odds.
This horse is in good form and looks to have been found a good opportunity here to strike for the first time at this level. The yard is going well and should take some beating.

Joannes at 20/1 may look like an outsider in the 14:45 at Newton Abbot on Thursday, but there are some reasons to consider him an each-way chance in this weak Conditional Jockey's Handicap Hurdle. Pipe's yard knows how to land a touch in modest races like this, especially with horses that look out of form on paper. He's reached for blinkers for the first time, which could sharpen Joannes up mentally.
A past Irish winner that is yet to fire in Blighty. Cheek pieces are reached for, which may keep him on the right line of fire.
Hard to see anything other than Mighty Fleur winning here today at Newton Abbot. It looks great value and ready for this. Worth a punt.
Finished a bit lame when making debut but improved from that run to finish 4th at Carlisle. This is a weaker race, so could perform vastly better.
Can Defy another hefty rise in the weights. Has improved markedly and can keep doing so. Beat some smart horses previously, and the form keeps getting boosted.

An inconsistent performer but indicative of the level. Therefore, this lad is a C&D winner and one of only two in the field with good form over the trip. Lacey is one of the more reliable trainers and had winners last week at Aintree. I don't know if Ben Sutton will ever ride out the claim, but he has won on this lad here previously, and a small bet is worth a go.

Lightinthewing is a course and distance winner who did so from a one-pound lower rating last year. Taking his ability to handle former ground on trust, he ran a decent third last time at Wincanton. If putting another good run together, he can be involved.
Absolutely loves it here and goes well fresh. Ground conditions are ideal and against 2 disappointing rivals is the value option.
Yard is flying and can go well with figures of 54 and may improve again to fight out the finish. Not a strong race on paper and may put experience to best use.

Call Me Legend boasts strong place form in better races and now drops into a winnable grade. Trained by the Hobbs-White team and ridden by Sean Houlihan, he has the stamina and determination for this trip. With form behind stronger opposition, he’s well-poised to go one better today.

Harpsichord showed a bit on debut when fourth at Southwell and looked like the type who’d improve with experience. Steps up in trip here, returns from a break, and goes handicapping off what could be a fair mark. With the trainer flying and a strong jockey combo in AW handicaps (46 runs, 17 wins (35%), +8pts @ 16% ROI), he’s one to keep onside.
Promising debut last time out when a decent 4th at Wolverhampton. Didn't get the best start but was staying on well. That was over 1m 1f, so today's step up in trip will suit.

Nivelles Magic is coming back after a long layoff, but the last time this happened, after 245 days, was a close 4th here at 150/1. Dan Horsford is now the trainer of this one, and it's very interesting today as, surprisingly, there is not a lot of course form in the field today. I think this one is good for at least a place.

4yo filly Countless Candy is on a handy mark 4lbs below her opening hc mark. Didn't quite stay the 1m4f lto so the drop back in trip seems ideal. Booking of amazing Rossa Ryan catches the eye and she should be in the mix here.

Sea Of Charm is the only course and distance winner in the field, winning off a mark of 54 back in 2021. She was also a runner-up over course and distance beaten a neck off a mark of 67 in 2022 and races off 56 today.
Only finished 8 of 11 here over C&D LTO last month. She is operating off a mark that is close to the last winning mark, and hoping the use of blinkers gives her the spark she needs.
Placed third first time out at Kempton. Now back after a 170+ days break and now under a shorter distance. Carries a lot of backing after a promising first time out.

Excuses at Wolves last time as she was forced out wide, but was very promising on debut the time before when very green, missing the break, but finishing well once the penny had dropped. That run was over course and distance, so has every chance back here today.
Havana Joy has been going very close of late, and the drop back in trip here is probably quite beneficial. Will have every chance here.

Thapa VC ran a fair race last time at Wolves despite racing a bit keenly and is now back down to a mark he can work with. Conditions suit nicely, he’s a C&D winner, and the yard have really stepped it up on the all-weather in recent seasons.

Not one to rely on with just 3 wins from 27 runs to date. Currently going through a barren run as it's now been 16 runs since the last win back in 2022. He is well handicapped, but hoping he can finally take advantage of the reducing mark.

If this had been at Newcastle, I would have been much stronger on Tomorrow Day. The consistent 4-year-old Adday gelding has form figures of 21323424 this year. Dropped a pound to 64, he is still 4 lbs above his last mark but should be good enough to go close in this company once again.
Midnightattheoasis has won his last 4 starts, with the last 2 coming over course and distance. He is up another 4 lb, but in his current form, he looks to have a great chance of going in again.

9yo irish gelding Recon Mission is on a more than dangerous mark 16lbs below his last winning mark from July 22. Only beaten by a neck lto over C&D when Midnightattheoasis made his 4 timer. Definitely will be in the mix here.

Take an EW chance as well here with 6yo gelding Harb. He was only a 3/4 length behind lto in the same race as my no 1 pick Recon Mission. Is 1lb below his last winning mark which was over C&D last November and holds every chance to go close here.
Clearly not a horse to be underestimated, especially being a 7-time C&D winner and still running off the last winning mark. If in the right mood, it will take some stopping.

Royal Accord did well to finish as close as she did at Bath last time after a slow start, beaten just over a length off 53. She’s improving with each run this season and now tries Polytrack for the first time. If she handles the surface, she looks a big danger.

This horse is friendless in the early market but looks like another good each-way bet to nothing on the card. The booking of Sean Levey certainly catches the eye since this is the AW track where he has the best strike rate (17%), and he's only been used by the stable 4 times before (providing one win and one place). Progeny of Mehmas also do particularly well at the course, and with Levey taking over from an apprentice, I'm expecting a more power-packed ride here, and he should be there or thereabouts.

Woodhay Whisper finished very nicely from the back of the field and looks like a genuine improver in this field (given the last race has been franked already). Should be able to do better here (has already gotten the better of Royal Accord).

Course winner who has doubts about today's 6f, but has kept on well in some of their 5f runs and family have won over 6/7f. Very good Aw jockey back up and shrewd training duo are 22 percent with their 3yo's here last 5 seasons, making current 10/1 solid Ew value in the race.

SARABI has switched stables which could be an edge worth keeping on side in this desperately low grade handicap. He did attract a fair amount of support on his last start for Jack Channon and with the services of Rossa Ryan called upon there is reason to be hopeful.

On ratings, this horse has a bit to find so this is just a small eachway, risky tip. Did show good early pace on that last run at Chelmsford, if showing the same good early pace today , it would be better suited to this particular course. Does need some improvement but the selection may yet have a bit more to offer. Very small eachway tip.

Hala Joza didn't run too badly in defeat last time out when finishing 6th over this distance at Wolverhampton in mid March , had his path blocked on more than one occasion when trying to make a forward run after sitting at the back of the pack , probably would have done better than finishing 6th had he got a better , clearer run through the race. From today's good draw, he should be able to get a better track position and hopefully avoids any traffic issues during the race. Still open to improvement so may do better today. At these odds, might be one to consider eachway.

Backer Bilk is steadily progressing, with a recent strong finish suggesting readiness for a breakthrough. Well positioned in the draw and running off a fair weight, this 3-year-old filly gets a good opportunity here. She should be prominent early and can prove hard to pass in this tightly-matched sprint.

Good stats for win and place for this trainer in this type of race. This 3-year-old looked a slow improver last season and could have more to offer, rated 59 now. Final start was best run, a keeping on third place finish.
3yo filly Spoilt had a good hc debut lto here at this course over 7f. Seems to be on a fair mark and the longer trip today should suit. Shouldn't be far away.

Muy Muy Loco raced a bit freely and looked one-paced over 7f here last time. But stepping up in trip could help him settle and finish better. On a fair opening mark based on his earlier form, and the trainer-jockey combo does well in AW handicaps (109 runs, 13 wins (12% ROI), +66pts @ 61% ROI). Bit to prove, but not without a shout if the new trip suits.

No show in their last two 2yo runs, but debut run in a decent class 4 maiden @ Newbury was not devoid of promise. Gets into first time handicap on 3yo return off very reasonable mark of 60, good apprentice up claiming 5lb and in hands of a shrewd trainer, making current 33/1 very good Ew value in the race.

This son of Dubawi was a 140,000 euro purchase last summer from a top French yard to David O'Meara. He has had one race (last summer) for his new yard and flopped in soft/heavy going, but his two previous races in France give optimism that he may be above his handicap mark. A wind operation over the winter will help with his breathing, so I'm taking a chance on him with decent chances. King Chaos and Cadarn are in the mix.

SEA LEGEND has joined trainer Jim Goldie who arrives in fine form. That coulds mean this new recruit is seen to good effect on his stable debut and in a flat handicap over a C/D where he has previously been successful he should be competitive.

Ninth Life showed real grit to get his head in front at Southwell last time and has gone well over this 10f trip before. He’s nicely treated on his best form and the trainer jockey combo has a good record on the AW, but coming off a long layoff does raise a question. Big chance if fit enough to fire.

Cusack looked like he had more to offer when finishing strongly to win over 7f here last time, and the step up in trip should bring out further improvement. He’s clearly heading the right way, the trainer’s in form, and the jockey combo does well in these races (50 runs, 10 wins (20%), +43pts @ 86% ROI).

Bruce Banner has been in decent form over C&D and backed up his Kempton win with a solid third off 58 last time. This looks a very winnable race with little depth, and if he runs to the same level again, he’s got a great chance of getting back to the winner’s enclosure.
Not beaten by far in 2 C/D outings last season as a 2-year-old. First run for a while, but ran well here fresh and on debut last September. Could break its maiden tag this evening.

Aoifes Thunder was well beaten on debut but should improve upon that, and she’s bred to do better with time and experience. She’s back from a break now and the yard has a fair record in non-handicaps on the all-weather, so wouldn’t be a surprise to see her outrun market expectations.

This will be the horse's third run at Newcastle. The first time, like today, was over 7 furlongs and was very green. Then it was stepped up in trip over a distance that looked too far but picked up experience. Today, with cheek pieces and a good jockey, I can see a big improvement.
Jowdah has hit the post in his last 3 outings, but after a bit of a break, he can break his duck and get his head in front. Looks the pick of the bunch here.

Showed a bit of promise on debut but couldn't quite get involved when it mattered. Returned from an absence last time out for second outing and ran well considering he was short of room when looking to get into position to challenge. However, did run on and although finished 5th, caught the eye. Will be better for that run and more improvement likely. Could get involved here at good odds.

Princess Amber ran a decent race on debut at Southwell, shaping like one who’ll come on for the experience and should appreciate the step up in trip. She’s up against some sharper types here but the yard does well in AW non-handicaps (39 runs, 7 wins (18%), +28pts @ 71% ROI), so she’s not one to rule out if taking a step forward.

Three uninspiring runs for Sir M Prescott as a 2yo, but the last one was the best @ Yarmouth. Interesting today on stable debut over this stiff mile which will suit, very under used jockey up and shrewd trainer best here with her 3yo's last 5 seasons, making current 40/1 decent Ew value in the race.
Things didn't go to plan last time for Jungle Land, but he won with loads of promise the time before. Great chance he's gonna bounce back today.

Paul Midgley's C&D winner Grant Wood finished second on his seasonal debut at Wolverhampton a month ago, and that run should have put him right. The six-year-old can take this off the reasonable mark of 85.

Flying Fletcher is a four year-old and has only won two of 13 starts so far but both wins were over course and distance. They were achieved from marks of 68 and 77 but the latter was a comfortable 3.5 length success so could be quite capable of scoring off OR83. Trained by Richard Fahey who often continues to steadily eke out improvement in a handicapper and is in his usual good form for this time of year with recent winners. Oisin Orr rides. Ran quite well on only previous return from a break in big field handicap at York. Slow starts have become a feature but could be just the ticket if they go off too hard. Looks a value bet for the win at 12-1.
Career best win last time and is worth an EW bet. Back running here at his favourite track and moved back up to 6F. Worth an EW bet.

Jenever was just touched off over 5f here when last seen in November and was well backed that day, suggesting confidence behind him. Steps back up to 6f now which should be fine, and he’s not badly treated at the weights. If he’s ready to go after the break, he looks a strong contender.

This C/D winner goes well here as last 2 runs show. Retains a decent mark of 87 in this grade 3, under used jockey up and good trainer who does very well in the sprinting sphere, best here with his 4yo plus last 5 seasons, making current 12/1 solid Ew value in the race.
Not in the best of form coming into this, but does have ability and a mark similar to the last winning mark. A drop down in class should make life a bit easier tomorrow.

ORMULULU stepped up in grade last time out on the tapeta at Southwell and didn't fare badly at all. Was a little unlucky in running, so could still fare better from a workable mark and hopefully gets a gap. If that opens this one could fire as the kick and pace are there to potentially take advantage if so.

Has been making steady progress with the latest just being done on the line. All its previous outings have been over longer trips than this evening, so there are question marks. But the trainer knows the horse better than me and gets my vote.

BOW STREET is the only horse with consistent form over this trip and course - the last time he ran here in this class he won with a higher RPR than any of these can produce and at a similar price in the betting as today (5/1 winner that day). Daniel Muscutt is fantastic on this surface and has won 20% of his races in the last 14 days so will be looking to strike again today!

Has won 3 times over 5f, including here at Newcastle in December. Bit of an absence when returning last time out to run a good 3rd here over 5f. Was hampered that day but has looked as though a step up to 6f will suit. Tudthorpe is in form and takes the ride for the first time.

Rooska is interesting being upped in trip after staying on late last time here over 7f. He obviously had some problems in training, running only once last season, but things seem to be back on track this time and hopefully he can get his first career win.
Awful run LTO, but the time before that he went very close over CD off 1 lb higher and in a better class of race.

The Seb Spencer trained Dale Swift ridden Odd Socks Havana recorded a double here over 7f & 8f off marks of 51 & 53 last April and that was the last time he won when trained by Rebecca Menzie. He races off 51 today and with conditions in his favour he can run a big race providing Dale can avoid traffic problems.
Turned back the clock with a useful effort LTO when 4 of 8 at Southwell last month and certainly no mug at this course, having scored 6 wins over C&D and operating just below last winning mark.

This gelding, a past course winner, has not triumphed in his last 15 races since 2024. He recently placed 10th out of 11 in a minor event at Wolverhampton, where he had a very slow start. On a positive note, the 6-year-old previously finished 6th and 4th in a couple of races here at Newcastle in March over 7.1 furlongs. Therefore, considering an each-way bet at 25/1 could be profitable if he can regain that competitive form.
In great consistent form at the moment, so don't need to look much further than this one for a selection. It should continue its run of good performances at this course tonight.

Just Typical has been holding his form well despite a busy spell, winning nicely off 54 then backing it up with a solid third off 56. He’s clearly in the groove and stays in similar company, so with no signs of tailing off, he’s got an obvious chance of going close again.

Coramento made a great start for his new yard when scoring comfortably here off 45, doing it with a bit in hand. The trainer’s in form and he looks like there’s more to come now he’s found his stride. Very much one to consider for the follow-up.

Winner over course and distance in November. Inconsistent since but ran well here a couple of times last month before poor effort over 7 furlongs last time. Would be no surprise to see him bounce back this evening back up in trip and down in grade.

There may be an element of sentiment as the horse is pretty much drawing his pension. It ran a fair 3rd in a classified event recently, and if it can transfer the form to this handicap, it's in with a shout. The stable is in good form, and I tend to think when these old ones show a bit, that is the time to be interested. If no show, forget from here on in.

Out of form right now, and it's been 11 runs since the last win last year. But he has course experience and is now running well below the last winning mark. After a rusty performance LTO, he should be ready to go.

An interesting looking class 3 handicap hurdle where i will be siding with Park Annonciade was last seen at Wetherby 14 days ago where finishing 7th/13 in a race that was not the best of run for Park Annonciade to be suited however S R B Crawford's gelded son of Masked Marvel remains with plenty of potential and a good analysis of this contest clearly showes Park Annonciade should have his favoured gallop at his disposal given the horses enrolled to run making him a very serious contender here currently operating on a mark 114 Park Annonciade looks poised to strike here and worth noting he is now operating on his last winning mark jockey J J Slevin takes the ride that being another positive factor and price at the time of writing represents very good E/W value must be taken seriously and accordingly . Respected .
Trainer Andrew Balding has yet to hit top form this season. Spell Master had a good first season and with top-jockey Oisin Murphy on board can run well.
